In Narva, the mayor asked for exceptions for families split by the border, while Estonia's interior minister said Russia runs intelligence and recruitment at the crossings and the Threod arson attempt was the last straw.
corroboration: ERR (two reports, 25 November); Hromadske on the Estonian prime minister's remark that rail could be next.
analysis: A rare public disagreement among Baltic governments, but over method and timing, not over the Russian threat itself. Latvia's decision will show whether a common Baltic line emerges.

title: Estonia's defence minister: Ukraine is not using Estonian airspace to attack Russia
summary: Defence Minister Martin Herem told the Riigikogu on 25 November that Ukrainian drones do not use Estonian airspace to strike Russia, that Ukraine never asked permission and that Estonia has asked it to stay out; strays happen because of jamming, countermeasures or weather. An unaffiliated MP had stated the opposite as fact. The Russian foreign ministry made the same accusation on 23 November. A Debunk.org study, reported by LRT, counted over 5,000 Kremlin-aligned articles pushing anti-Baltic narratives from January to October, with Baltic complicity in drone strikes the most common.
corroboration: ERR; Debunk.org study via LRT and 77.lt.
analysis: Both sides agree some drones stray into Estonian airspace; nobody has published evidence that this is deliberate or permitted. The accusation matters because Moscow ties it to its 'open war' warning.

title: How a Kaliningrad alert became a 'NATO attack' online
summary: An analysis by Repsense, reported by BNS and LRT on 23 November, found that after the 21 November air-raid alert in Kaliningrad, whose governor said an object came from the Lithuanian side but posed no threat, three English-language X accounts produced most of about 450 posts claiming a NATO or Ukrainian attack from Lithuania. Russian state media relayed only part of the governor's statement. Lithuania's foreign ministry denied any attack on 22 November.
corroboration: LRT/BNS citing Repsense; earlier Euromaidan Press reporting of explosions in Baltiysk remains unverified.
analysis: Shows how a local alert can be inflated into an escalation story without any official Russian claim. Reports of blasts in Baltiysk the same night are still not confirmed.

title: Seven EU leaders urge curbs on Russian travel; OPCW rejects Russia
summary: Lithuania's president and the prime ministers of Latvia, Estonia, Poland, Denmark, Finland and Sweden asked the Commission and the European Council to propose limits on non-essential travel by Russians and to stop visas for Russian and Belarusian athletes. At the OPCW conference in The Hague, states rejected Russia's bid for the Executive Council on 24 November and elected Estonia and Poland; Latvia cited Ukraine's count of over 14,000 Russian chemical-weapons violations.
corroboration: LRT; LSM.
analysis: Political and diplomatic pressure, not a security incident. Moscow has called Estonia's closure a 'new Iron Curtain' and may answer the travel push in similar terms.

title: Drone briefly enters Latvian airspace near the Russian border
summary: Latvia's armed forces said an unidentified drone entered Latvian airspace in the early hours of 27 November. An actual-threat alert was sent to phones in Ludza municipality shortly before 03:00 and lifted within minutes, followed by a lower-level alert for Balvi municipality that ended around 03:29. NATO fighters and an interceptor drone were deployed. At about the same time, the governor of Russia's Leningrad region said more than 40 drones had been downed in an attack on the region.
corroboration: Reuters and LSM from the Latvian armed forces; no attribution yet.
analysis: Latvia has had several strays this year, some of them Ukrainian drones pushed off course by Russian jamming, and the timing points to the Leningrad attack. Until Latvia attributes it, this is an airspace incident, not evidence of a Russian probe.

title: Poland's foreign minister: downing missiles over Ukraine would be self-defence
summary: Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said on Polish radio on 25 November that shooting down Russian missiles or drones over Ukraine at Kyiv's request would be necessary defence, because an approaching missile is a direct threat. Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said NATO is not in favour and hopes the planned no-fly zone along the eastern border, 12 to several dozen kilometres deep, will take effect in late December or early January. Ukraine's ambassador said Kyiv shares real-time missile and drone data with Poland.
corroboration: Euromaidan Press (Ukrainian outlet) citing Polsat and RMF FM; Bloomberg's earlier report that Poland raised the idea at NATO still rests on unnamed sources.
analysis: Sikorski's remarks make Poland's position clearer than Bloomberg's sourcing did, but there is still no NATO decision and Warsaw's concrete step remains a zone over its own territory.

title: Weekend GPS interference also hit Tallinn, Helsinki and Åland
summary: Dagens Nyheter and Danish analysis of gpsjam.org data, reported by European Pravda on 26 November, show that interference on 21–23 November was strongest around Stockholm but also affected Gotland, Tallinn, Helsinki and the Åland Islands; Tallinn and Helsinki still showed heavy interference on 23 November. Sweden's Transport Agency called it serious and found no natural cause, but no state was named. A Danish naval officer said suspicion falls on Russia. The same weekend a drone, which Ukraine's president said Ukraine sent, hit the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland.
corroboration: Dagens Nyheter and DR via European Pravda; Yle on the Sparta II.
analysis: A wider footprint for one episode, not a new episode. Some interference may be linked to Russian defences against Ukrainian drones and ship strikes, but nobody has shown that, and the effect on civil aviation is the same either way.

title: Latvia delays its Russia-border decision; Lithuania sees no need to close
summary: Latvia's prime minister, Andris Kulbergs, has asked the foreign and transport ministries to assess closing crossings with Russia, including the effect on transit, with the issue expected in the week of 30 November rather than on 26 November. Latvia's border guard chief has warned that traffic will shift to Latvia once Estonia closes its road crossings on 1 December. In Lithuania, new border guard chief Donatas Škarnulis told LRT there is no need to close the Russian crossings now, while President Gitanas Nausėda called Estonia's move appropriate and did not rule out similar steps.
corroboration: Delfi via Bytes Europe and Glavnoe; LRT/BNS.
analysis: Three neighbours, three approaches. The disagreement is about timing and cost, and Russia's foreign ministry has already protested to Estonia, calling the closure an anti-Russian stunt.

title: Moscow: no plans to attack NATO, but NATO 'openly preparing' for war
summary: At her 20 November briefing, foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said Russia has no intention of attacking NATO states and has proposed mutual security guarantees, while also saying NATO is openly preparing for war with Russia and noting that both sides have nuclear weapons. Three days later the ministry warned that Estonia was bringing the situation to the brink of open war, and on 23 November it protested Estonia's border closure.
corroboration: TASS; Ukrainska Pravda on the protest to Estonia.
analysis: Reassurance and warning in the same week is a familiar pattern. Lithuania's threat assessment judges Russia by its rebuilding of military capacity, not by such statements; neither line changes that judgement.

title: Poland: false Kaliningrad narratives reached millions
summary: A public summary by the Global Security Centre, a Warsaw risk firm, cites Poland's state counter-disinformation centre as estimating that false narratives about the 21 November Kaliningrad alert reached at least 19 million people. It also notes that Russia's ambassador, summoned over the three Kh-101 missiles that fell in Poland on 20 November, said they were not Russian.
corroboration: GSC summary of Polish official estimates; Lithuanian and Polish fact-checks of the Kaliningrad claim earlier this week.
analysis: Shows the reach of a story that had no official Russian backing. The audience figure is an estimate, and the firm's own risk ratings are its judgement.

title: Estonia issues drone alert; Latvia reinforces its eastern air defence
summary: Estonia's Defence Forces sent an air-threat alert to six southern and south-eastern counties at 06:40 on 27 November and lifted it at 07:24; NATO fighters were scrambled. The alert came hours after an unidentified drone briefly entered Latvia over Ludza, while Russia's Leningrad region governor reported a large drone attack there. Latvia's armed forces have sent extra air defence units to the eastern border and warned that more foreign drones could enter.
corroboration: ERR via LB.ua; Euronews citing the Latvian armed forces, LSM and AFP; Bytes Europe citing LRT.
analysis: Both alerts fit the pattern of Ukrainian long-range drones flying near the Baltic borders, sometimes diverted by Russian jamming. Neither country has attributed them, and no damage was reported.

title: Russia's OSCE envoy: NATO bringing the world 'closer to nuclear war'
summary: Speaking in Vienna on 26 November, Russia's permanent representative to the OSCE, Dmitry Polyansky, said NATO military activity near Russia's borders and the involvement of some NATO countries in attacks on Russian civilian ships in the Baltic bring the world closer to nuclear war. He claimed allied drills near Kaliningrad aim to rehearse seizing the region and cited the drone strike on the cargo ship Sparta II.
corroboration: TASS; Newsweek, which notes Lithuania calls the drills readiness training.
analysis: A familiar Russian line, now tied to the Ukrainian strikes on Russian shipping. No evidence is offered that NATO states took part in those strikes, and the drills are publicly announced.

title: Kremlin: Ukraine is spreading the war to the Baltic
summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 26 November that Ukraine is trying to spread the war to the Baltic and Mediterranean seas, calling it dangerous. He was responding to a joint statement after US President Donald Trump met NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, which urged Russia to avoid widening the war; Trump later said both Russia and Ukraine must avoid such actions.
corroboration: An aggregated summary of Reuters and Politico reports; the original articles could not be read for this edition.
analysis: The exchange shows the Baltic Sea becoming a theatre of the Russia–Ukraine war through ship strikes, which raises the risk of incidents near Baltic and Finnish waters even without any plan to attack NATO.

title: IISS: Russia-linked sabotage in Europe up 16% in a year
summary: A study by the International Institute for Strategic Studies, published on 26 November, counts a 16% rise in Russia-linked sabotage incidents in Europe from October 2025 to September 2026. Poland accounted for about a quarter of incidents, and Germany and the Baltic states for about a fifth each; arson and bomb attacks roughly doubled and five attempted assassinations were recorded. The study says the campaign has not achieved a strategic effect but warns a mass-casualty incident is becoming more possible.
corroboration: LB.ua; Kyiv Independent via Yahoo.
analysis: An independent count that supports the Lithuanian baseline's description of hybrid threats. It covers a past period, so it does not change today's counts.

title: Report: Russian warship suspected of jamming GPS on UK flights
summary: The Telegraph reported on 24 November, citing analysis by the aviation intelligence group Hexbird first published by the i paper, that a GPS outage on 9 November affected about 140 flights, with a likely source over the North Sea where a Russian warship was escorting sanctioned cargo ships. Hexbird said its analysis neither identifies nor rules out the convoy. Anadolu quotes an unnamed senior British defence source as sceptical; the UK government did not comment.
corroboration: The Telegraph via Yahoo; Anadolu Agency citing British media.
analysis: The headlines run ahead of the evidence: the source itself does not attribute the outage. It also lies outside the Baltic region, so it is not counted here.

title: Lithuania: at least 5% of GDP on defence may be needed until 2035–2040
summary: Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said on 27 November that Lithuania will need at least 5% of GDP for defence for a decade or longer, possibly 5.5%, to build a national division and strengthen air, maritime and border defence. The government has proposed 5% of GDP, over €4.8 billion, for next year.
corroboration: LRT/BNS.
analysis: A long-term planning signal consistent with the baseline's view that the threat is about Russia's rebuilt capacity over years, not an imminent attack.
